shell.json: Every page here also answers ?format=json, and every form also accepts a JSON body, so a test can drive this console without a browser.
shell.notStamped: (not a stamped build — this process is a checkout, and the build number is when it started)
shell.open.text: This console is not protected. The gate is OFF, so nothing here checks a credential — and nothing else in this service does either: the username typed at the sign-in screen is the identity in every token it issues. Anyone who can reach this port can revoke every token and change what the next one contains. That is fine on a laptop or a compose network and is not fine on a public address. Say who may get in on
shell.open.after: , which draws every setting behind this page.
shell.brandTip: This console is showing the trust realm "{name}" (id: {id}). Its issuer identifier, in every protocol (#523), is {issuer}: every SAML
shell.brandTip.after: , every identity provider entityID and every JWT's iss.
shell.backToFiltered: Back to {label} — the filter and page you came from
shell.noSession.text: Nobody is signed in on this browser. This console needs a session of its own — it is an ordinary OpenID Connect client of this service, sts-admin-console in the registry — so every page of it will run the sign-in flow again.
shell.bootstrap.text: Signed in as {who}, and holding both roles because {boot} has not signed in to this console yet. Until this service's bootstrap administrator first signs in here, anyone who signs in has the whole console (admin.openWhenEmpty). From that moment only members of {read} and {write} may use it — so grant yourself a role on
shell.bootstrap.after: first if you will need one.
shell.openRoster.text: Signed in as {who}, and holding both roles because NOBODY HOLDS EITHER. This console always asks you to sign in — but neither {read} nor {write} has a single member, and while that is true anyone who signs in has the whole console. This service has no password to bootstrap an administrator with, which is why the empty roster opens rather than closes (admin.openWhenEmpty).
shell.openRoster.after: and the roster is enforced from that moment — including against you, so grant yourself one first.
shell.unclaimed: Signed in as {who}, holding no console role: this console has not been claimed yet. In product mode only the bootstrap administrator, {named, select, yes {{boot}} other {the bootstrap administrator}}, signing in with its password, can use this console until it does. Nobody else holds a role until one is granted, and a sign-in as {named, select, yes {{boot}} other {the bootstrap administrator}} by a federation partner, a certificate, a wallet or a Kerberos ticket does not count.
shell.ok.write: . Every control on these pages is yours.
shell.ok.read: . This is a READ-ONLY view: the forms are drawn so that you can see what they do, and posting one is refused. {group} is the role that changes that.
shell.ok.logout: signs you out of everything this service holds — every protocol at once — and
shell.ok.operator: is the operator's view of the same lists, for somebody else.
shell.foreign: Your session belongs to the trust realm {name} ({id}) and this console follows it into every realm, because the two console roles are groups in the one shared directory. The protocol endpoints do not: in this realm /oauth2/authorize, /wsfed and the two SAML profiles see no session at all and would ask you to sign in.
shell.retiring: This realm is {state, select, stuck {stuck half way through its removal} other {being removed}}.
shell.retiring.after: says what is refused and how to finish.
shell.refresh.title: Load this page again. Everything in this console is live state held in memory.
shell.menu.title: Your own account. This console is read as {user}, and the two controls in here are the ones about YOU rather than about the service.
shell.menu.account.title: Your own account in the user portal — your password, your authenticator app, your security keys and the applications you can be signed in to. It is a different application from this console and it signs you in with the session you already hold, so nothing is typed again. The link is to the portal of the realm you signed in through, because that is where your account is, whichever realm you are reading.
shell.signOut.title: End this console session and the sign-on session behind it. You are signed in as {user}. Signing out of the console alone would not sign you out: the next page would run the sign-in flow, meet the sign-on session that is still live and let you straight back in.
